title: Learning Universal Costs via Multi-Observation Inverse Optimal Transport
summary: Classical Inverse Optimal Transport (IOT) typically infers a cost function from a single observed transport plan, which may be sensitive to noise and observational biases in practice. To address this limitation, we propose the Multi-Observation Inverse Optimal Transport (M-IOT) framework, which learns a universal cost function from multiple transport plans. We reformulate the resulting bilevel optimization problem into a tractable single-level convex program and characterize the existence and geometric structure of the optimal solution set.
